value: In the past year, Swiss 8 has significantly advanced its mission to empower veterans by focusing on the delivery of the Recalibr8 Fundamentals program. This online initiative provided identity transition and holistic health training to 2400 veterans, exceeding our set targets. The program was designed to enhance mental resilience and foster a life of purpose for people transitioning through a significant life milestone. By offering this course free of charge, we ensured that veterans had access to crucial tools for managing their mental health and personal growth, directly aligning with our mission to reshape veterans' mental health care. The success of Recalibr8 Fundamentals not only helped in building a supportive community but also in promoting the values of mentalism, correspondence, and balance as outlined in our guiding principles. Veterans engaged with the content through digital platforms, fostering a network of support and shared experiences. This year's focus has laid a strong foundation for our longterm goals, demonstrating our commitment to becoming Australia's most effective ESO for veterans' holistic health and contributing to the global standard for veterans' mental health care.

value: The principal activity of the Gynaecological Cancer Research, Education and Development Society Limited during the year was a charity whose purpose is to advance health by undertaking the following gynaecological oncology activities: Maintaining and operating the database of gynaecological cancer for the Queensland Tophoblast Centre at the Royal Brisbane Women s Hospital in Brisbane, Queensland. Providing training and workshops for medical professionals regarding gynaecological oncology to ensure that they have the highest level of skill when carrying out their duties. Provide education seminars to the public regarding gynaecological oncology, and the risks, prevention, and treatment for gynaecological cancer. Undertaking research into the causes, diagnosis, treatment and/or management of gynaecological cancer and publishing the results of that research. Enabling medical practitioners to attend and participate at international gynaecological oncology conferences that will further train and develop professional skill for and knowledge of gynaecological oncology.

value: LCANZ s mission is to build and sustain a transnational organisation, providing professional development, advocacy and peer support for all members. Our mission commits us to the empowerment of breastfeeding women and their families/whanau. We endeavour to advise and make representations to relevant State and National Government authorities on issues relating to breastfeeding and human lactation and the profession of lactation consultancy. Lyn Slatter worked tirelessly in her commitment to the profession of IBCLC® and to the promotion of breastfeeding. Countless mothers and babies benefited from her knowledge, experience, and wisdom. Lyn was a great mentor and role model for many IBCLC®s, midwives, and other health professionals and had a great capacity for compassion, wonderful clinical skills in caring for mothers, babies and families. In her honour and in recognition of her contribution to the profession, the Lyn Slatter Memorial Scholarship has been established. At the request of Lyn and her family, this scholarship is to assist with the cost of sitting the IBLCE® exam for the first time.

value: Systems Chemistry Australia partnered with Sena Ltd in Reykjavik, Iceland to support the latter and the cochairs; the Chairperson Prof. Pall Thordarson, Prof. Krishna Damodaran (Iceland) and Prof. Thorfinnur Gunnlaugsson (Ireland) in running the International Symposium of Macrocyclic and Supramolecular Chemistry (ISMSC) in Reykjavik, Iceland 2529th June 2023. Sena managed the conference, collecting registration fees and sponsorship with Sena, Systems Chemistry Australia (on behalf of Pall Thordarson) and the other two cochairs splitting the risk/profits of the conference.. The conference was a success with over 500 people attending. Sena intended to complete the finances in early 2024 but delays with getting some outstanding invoices paid delayed this to the end of 2024 with the latest estimate that Systems Chemistry Australia will receive around $2500 from the surplus of this meeting. As a promotional event for systems chemistry and supramolecular chemistry the ISMSC in Iceland was a resounding success. Over 20 scientists from Australia were amongst the 500 people at the meeting. Systems Chemistry Australia also gave support for running the NSW Student Computational Chemistry a topic of significant importance within systems chemistry Meeting in Kiama, NSW on 1012th July 2023 with Dr. Junming Ho (UNSW) as the chair. The conference itself was a success with 45 people attending and the conference making a$4100 split between the FY2223 and FY2324. The organisation also continued to be a named supporter of the Opendatafit / supramolecular.org project. This project has now served over 30,000 users and + 80,000 citations in the literature from scientists around the world.

value: We improved nature conservation outcomes locally through securing the registration of several properties in the Land for Wildlife program, promoting nature conservation to individuals and the wider community (site visits, presentations, a local 'Picnic for Nature' and distribution of TreeTroff birdbaths in partnership with WIRES), and continued delivery of bush regeneration services on public and private lands by contractors and volunteers. We monitored the granting of Exploration Licences, the activities of mining companies and released the results from a community Land Use Survey conducted in conjunction with Southern Cross University. To assist with improved outcomes for koalas, we provided support for the proposed Great Koala National Park and advice via representation on a Community Advisory Panel established by the NSW Government. Members were also active in the local council's Koala Working Group.

Fostered the Ukrainian language, poetry, literature, songs and music through this weekly radio program; and advanced the Ukrainian Performing Arts and our Culture through promotion to our community and all mainstream listeners (both in Australia and overseas). value: The community supports the work of the priest and ensures that Sunday Mass services are provided every week. This is especially important for older Hungarians who may find English language masses more difficult to understand. We have volunteers who help by transporting elderly to the weekly mass service and will also help the priest by visiting the sick and elderly who may be in hospital, nursing home or has home care but is unable to attend services. The monthly coffee afternoons and occasional lunches help to foster a greater sense of community and allow young nd old to engage with the culture.

value: The main activity is religious activity through the provision of financial resources and services to the Lutheran Church of Australia (LCA). LLL is a Religious Charitable Development Fund (RCDF) and as a charitable financial institution it provides loans and grants to LCA entities. LLL accepts investments from individuals and businesses who wish to support the charitable purposes of the LLL and whom consideration of profit is not of primary relevance. The organisation also operate a number of financial support services to the LCA. Due to the nature of the work of the LCA, the services provided enable a range of ministries to be supported, providing direct benefit to the promotion of religion while also supporting welfare and social services that the LCA engages in.

value: Forever Home Pet Rescue is a registered, not for profit and responsible No Kill rescue group dedicated to animal welfare and the rescue and rehabilitation of homeless, abandoned and neglected pets saved from local pounds and shelters. When pets arrive at Forever Home Pet Rescue they are placed into loving foster homes where they will remain until they find their Forever Home , however long that takes as we have a no kill policy. All pets are available for adoption once they complete their mandatory quarantine period. All pets will have all their vet work completed whilst in the care of Forever Home Pet Rescue and will be desexed, vaccinated, microchipped, wormed and flea treated by time of adoption. Some come in needing more extensive vet work which they will receive in our care. Every attempt is made to match the pet with the perfect family. Forever Home Pet Rescue offers ongoing education, advice and support to all adopters. The adoption fees and donations are the only funding Forever Home Pet Rescue receives to assist in continuing to rehome our pets

value: CAPDA has been operating in Tanzania for 15 years. We aim to bring about sustainable improvements in the lives of PWDs, their families and carers, and over the years we have found that the best way to do this is to build the capacity of local disability care organisations, principally but not exclusively through training programmes delivered by visiting health professionals. With the exception of the first two years of the pandemic, these delivery/monitoring visits have occurred twice yearly for between four and five weeks each time. Our development philosophy ensures that projects are developed in conjunction with the local providers, and in this we are aided by a local citizen who acts as CAPDA's liaison in Moshi. While our funds are mainly donations from Australians, we have also been successful in winning and acquitting grants from governments and other authorities, and to that end we have a comprehensive suite of development policies.

value: We are a communityled network dedicated to reducing suicide rates and minimising its devastating impact on individuals, families, and communities across our regions. Our approach is rooted in the belief that strong, connected communities are essential to preventing suicide and supporting those affected by it. Our mission is to empower local groups, organisations, and individuals with the resources, education, and training they need to recognise the signs of suicide risk, provide support, and foster meaningful conversations around mental health. We aim to create a culture of openness, understanding, and collaboration that will help reduce stigma, increase awareness, and ultimately save lives.

value: The first part of the year, with the hub doors still financed and open, we were able to still assist local residents with the recovery of their homes via donations and grants received. Once the hub doors closed in the second half, we have been expending successful grants received to provide the following: months. Our completed projects have included: Community Consultation Series was completed in late 2023 Purchase of shipping container stored in carpark of local high school out of flood zone. Purchase of $25,000 worth of cleaning and response equipment (stored in this container) ready for community use during next response phase. An asset register has been created and all equipment items have been engraved with an asset number. Creation of online equipment library via our website, allowing for userfriendly borrowing and tracking of items. Creation of website allowing for interaction by donors, volunteers and residents Purchase of $22,000 custombuilt BBQ Trailer bought to help in response phase and for fundraising activities. Purchase of ten CB radios to allow for better communication during response phase.

value: Our church s charitable work has been instrumental in furthering our overall mission to spread faith, serve the community, and promote spiritual growth and wellbeing. Through various initiatives, we have remained committed to our core values of compassion, love, and community support. Faith in Action: Our outreach programs have helped provide for the spiritual needs of the community by offering weekly worship services, Bible study groups, and different programs. These initiatives have fostered a strong sense of belonging and spiritual enrichment among congregants and newcomers alike. Community Care: We have organised and supported a range of communityfocused efforts. This includes programs for preschool kids, food hamper distribution, clothing donations, and other practical help that have provided relief to vulnerable individuals and families. Youth and Family Development: Our children s ministry, youth programs have helped foster personal development and resilience in our younger members. These programs have been designed to provide moral guidance and leadership skills, strengthening our mission of raising future faith leaders. Global Impact: We have extended our mission beyond local boundaries, contributing to disaster relief efforts and supporting international mission trips. This reflects our commitment to serve as instruments of peace and hope both locally and globally. In every initiative, we have aimed to embody our mission of faith, love, and service. By remaining attuned to the needs of our congregation and broader community, we continue to pursue our vision of creating a more compassionate and spiritually enriched world.

value: In 2024, Theatre Works continued to deliver on its mission to support independent artists, develop new Australian work, and provide accessible opportunities for audiences to engage with contemporary theatre and performance. Through its coproducing and presenting model, Theatre Works delivered a significant annual program of productions, developments, creative residencies, public programs, and artist support initiatives across the Theatre Works precinct, including the Main Theatre, Explosives Factory and TWiSK rehearsal space. The organisation supported hundreds of independent artists through paid employment, presentation opportunities, mentorship, technical and producing support, and access to affordable creative infrastructure. Theatre Works prioritised the development and presentation of original Australian stories, diverse artistic voices, and independent creative practice. The organisation also expanded audience engagement through accessible ticket pricing, education initiatives, regional touring partnerships, artist talks, workshops, and community events. During the year, Theatre Works completed major redevelopment works to improve accessibility, rehearsal facilities, artist amenities, and longterm sustainability of the venue. These improvements strengthen the organisation s capacity to support artists and audiences into the future. Despite ongoing financial pressures impacting the broader arts sector, Theatre Works maintained strong audience attendance, high levels of artistic activity, and continued investment in independent artists and cultural outcomes for Victoria.

value: LGBTIQ+ identifying people (being those who identify as lesbian, gay, bisexual, transgender, intersex, queer, and/or otherwise as gender and/or sexuality diverse) who face distress caused by discrimination, harassment, and bullying received, particularly those involved in sport. LGBTIQ+ identifying people disproportionately suffer from distress by virtue of them being LGBTIQ+ identifying. Specifically in sport, LGBTQI+ identifying people face unique structural discrimination and barriers. Recent research indicates that only 6% of LGBTQI+ identifying people are involved in a team sport, and 80% of Australians have experienced or witnessed LGBTQI+ discrimination in sport. These findings highlight that homophobia and transphobia remain a significant issue in sporting environments. Pride Cup undertakes the following projects and activities to reduce minority stress and structural discrimination suffered by LGBTQI+ people: 1. Pridethemed sporting events to activate community awareness & raise visibility; this includes running marquee events and Pride Cups (which are rainbow themed matches). 2. Education programs delivered to players, coaches & the broader community to tackle LGBTQI+ based discrimination, build empathy & promote acceptance; 3. Capacitybuilding to empower communities (through sporting clubs) to run their own events & lead initiatives supporting LGBTQI+ inclusion; 4. Partnership development to scale our growth & amplify impact through collaboration; and 5. Positive storytelling designed to increase the visibility of LGBTQI+ people, allyship and LGBTQI+ inclusion.

value: The Australia Alevi Cultural Centre (AACC) provides social, cultural, and religious services, as well as organizes various recreational activities for its members and the wider community. To enhance community awareness and participation in cultural, social, and religious functions, AACC employs a range of formal and informal communication tools, including letters, emails, SMS alerts, and AACC's Facebook page. value: The Flicker of Hope Foundation Ltd (FOH) aims to raise much needed funds to support research into and awareness of NF. FOH contributes funds raised to support researchers in their quest to find positive treatments and solutions to improve the quality of life for those impacted by NF. FOH through its fund raising efforts has helped to raise awareness in the community of NF. FOH has made great progress in achieving its aims over the past five years. FoH has raised over $3,000,000 in this period to support the following research projects into NF: >TiNT trial a trial of trametinib in children and adolescents with NF1 to treat plexiform neurofibromas and optic pathway gliomas. This research is being conducted by the Murdoch Children s Research Institute. >ctDNA NF1 project a project to explore the feasibility of early detection of Malignant Peripheral Nerve Sheath Tumours (MPNSTs) using a blood test. Partnering in this project are The Royal Children s Hospital, The Royal Melbourne Hospital and Peter MacCallum Cancer Centre. >Blood Pressure Monitoring Joint research project between The Royal Children s Hospital and Murdoch Children s Research Institute for blood pressure monitoring of children and adolescents with NF. >FOH initiative, collaborating with The Florey Institute of Neuroscience and Mental Health to conduct world leading, ground breaking research into autism, cognitive and behavioural issues in people with NF1. >Researching for an NF cure Associate Professor Aaron Schindeler is heading up a new research project aiming to achieve a CURE for NF. The project is being led by a team of researchers from The Children s Hospital at Westmead, Children s Medical Research Institute and The Australian National University. This is an exciting research project for the NF community. >A pioneering NF2 medical research project Dr Jim Whittle from The Walter and Eliza Hall Institute is establishing a registry of information of Australian patients with NF2 vestibular schwannomas (or acoustic neuromas) and other tumours. This registry will provide a framework to conduct clinical trials and identify new treatments, including evaluating the use of Bevacizumab in Australian patients with acoustic neuromas. >Reproductive decision making Research led by RNSH NF Team aimed at supporting reproductive decision making for people with NF. FOH continues to explore opportunities to work with researchers to identify positive treatments and solution to help improve the quality of life for those impacted by NF.

value: We have engaged over 50 professional artists and business people, supported over 250 performers, 350 community workshop participants and connected with 16 businesses. To top it all off we have also been seen by over 3500 audience members. Our work has been shared all over Australia and Internationally through our I Dance Film Festival and our own dance films. We were thrilled to represent dance and disability in the inaugural Uncharted Festival celebrating innovation and technology and to run our Pleiades program facilitating cross mentoring for 21 women of all ages, backgrounds and abilities. Our Sirius program reflecting the brightest star in the sky, enabled capacity building for our organisation and team to undertake training in LGBTQIA+ and Disability awareness and to invite internationally renowned LGBTQIA+ and Disability leaders to speak with the ACT community. We launched Stellar Step UP! supporting 7 new dance and exercise classes for people across the ACT of CaLD, First Nations and disability backgrounds. We also launched the BOLD Mingle program working with migrant elders to offer dance and exercise classes. These have become the highlight of the week for many of us and have also enabled us to directly connect with many of the brilliant classical India dancers in the ACT. Our BOLD Access program offered access and inclusion for the BOLD Festival will support of Events ACT and we become the only organisation in the ACT offering access options for Festivals. Outside of the ACT we continued our Gemini program in partnership with Singapore s Diverse Abilities Dance Collective and dived into Virtual View, an international dance exchange that explores the potential of Extended Reality (XR) in the interplay between body, identity and crosscultural exchange. Our annual performance offering A Stellar Lineup grew to encompass more groups and over 120 performers with Auslan, captioning and Audio Description. This is a huge achievement for a small organisation.

We were thrilled to represent dance and disability in the inaugural Uncharted Festival celebrating innovation and technology and to run our Pleiades program facilitating cross mentoring for 21 women of all ages, backgrounds and abilities. Our Sirius program reflecting the brightest star in the sky, enabled capacity building for our organisation and team to undertake training in LGBTQIA+ and Disability awareness and to invite internationally renowned LGBTQIA+ and Disability leaders to speak with the ACT community. We launched Stellar Step UP! supporting 7 new dance and exercise classes for people across the ACT of CaLD, First Nations and disability backgrounds. We also launched the BOLD Mingle program working with migrant elders to offer dance and exercise classes. These have become the highlight of the week for many of us and have also enabled us to directly connect with many of the brilliant classical India dancers in the ACT. Our BOLD Access program offered access and inclusion for the BOLD Festival will support of Events ACT and we become the only organisation in the ACT offering access options for Festivals. Outside of the ACT we continued our Gemini program in partnership with Singapore s Diverse Abilities Dance Collective and dived into Virtual View, an international dance exchange that explores the potential of Extended Reality (XR) in the interplay between body, identity and crosscultural exchange. Our annual performance offering A Stellar Lineup grew to encompass more groups and over 120 performers with Auslan, captioning and Audio Description. This is a huge achievement for a small organisation.

value: IEF provides financial support for the Mentawai Cultural Education Foundation (YPBM), a First Nations-led organisation designing and managing Indigenous education programs for Mentawai students aged between ages 7-18. Through a network of cultural learning hubs, students are taught in Mentawai's Sarereiket and Sabirut dialects, with hands-on learning covering topics such as language, cultural arts, forest foods, sustainable use of resources and economic growth opportunity. More than 60% of students enrolled are females. Executed via a robust and efficacious budget, 30-40 students are educated at each learning hub on a one-day per week basis, over 12 months of the year. Additionally, IEF provides financial support to the Ranu Welum Foundation in Central Kalimantan. Indigenous and female-led, Ranu Welum is driven by a team of young Dayak working to preserve their culture, protect the forests and fight for Dayak's Indigenous rights.

value: Our charity, Ladies Like To Lunch, is dedicated to supporting women affected by cancer in South Western Sydney. Every initiative we undertake is designed to empower these women, improve their quality of life, and foster a sense of community and connection. Achieving Our Mission: Wellness Programs: We successfully launched South Western Sydney s first 12week oncology exercise program in partnership with SWSLHD Liverpool Cancer Services. This initiative helps cancer patients regain strength, improve mental wellbeing, and enhance their recovery journey. Care Package Program: Since 2019, we ve distributed personalized care packages filled with thoughtfully selected items designed to comfort and support women undergoing treatment. These packages not only meet physical needs but also show our community s care and solidarity. Support Events: Through events like the Pink Ribbon Luncheon, we ve raised funds to directly support local cancer services, including the Liverpool Wellness Centre, while creating opportunities to celebrate resilience and foster connections among cancer warriors and their families. Advocacy and Community Voice: By serving as a Consumer Representative on the ACRF OASIS Committee, we ensure that the voices of cancer patients and their families are heard in decisionmaking processes, advocating for programs and research that directly improve patient outcomes. Collaboration with Local Businesses: Partnering with organisations we ve been able to deliver unique support initiatives, such as Mother s Day celebrations and wellnessfocused products, further enriching the lives of those we serve. Impact: Our work has provided practical, emotional, and physical support to countless women navigating the challenges of cancer. By focusing on wellness, connection, and advocacy, we re making tangible progress toward our mission of empowering women and fostering a stronger, more supportive community.

value: Recruiting Young and Diverse Stem Cell Donors The TLR Foundation is proud to be an official charity partner of Stem Cell Donors Australia to recruit new donors aged 1835. This year, our recruitment program became operational with inperson recruitment events for students at universities, such as the University of Sydney and the University of New South Wales, as well as events for young professionals in corporate graduate programs in companies across Sydney. By using simple cheek swabs for registration, the process could not be easier. These efforts are helping ensure every patient has a better chance of finding a lifesaving match. Raising Awareness and Educating Future Donors TLR launched targeted video campaigns and social media advertising to address the widespread lack of awareness about stem cell donation. By demystifying the donation process and focusing on transparency, we are recruiting committed donors who understand the lifechanging impact they could have on someone with blood cancer. This approach continues to attract young, dedicated individuals to the registry and bring hope to patients in need. Supporting Cancer Nurses Through our fundraising efforts, we are proud to support cancer nurses through perpetual scholarships. Our first scholarship, the Trace Richey Nursing Scholarship at the University of Sydney, has already helped two nurses pursue their Master of Cancer & Haematology Nursing. In 2024, we made significant progress towards fully funding our second perpetual scholarship, the Allan Frenkel Nursing Scholarship, which will double our efforts to create a lasting legacy, helping generations of nurses become specialists in blood cancer care. Advancing Research into Graft vs Host Disease (GvHD) TLR continues to support the GvHD research group at the Illawarra Health and Medical Research Institute (IHMRI) at the University of Wollongong. We provide research grants and share our personal experience with GvHD to help guide the team s work and assist with securing funding. This partnership underscores our commitment to improving outcomes for patients undergoing stem cell transplants.

value: Our project with Global Development Group is a COW BANK. It loan families a pregnant cow that they are required look after whilst its pregnant. When the calf is born, the family keep the baby and the project take the cow back (after the calf has been weaned) and it is reentered into the cow breeding program. Through GDG,Cows for Communities provides an opportunity to break the poverty cycle through cattle ownership, rather than a direct handout. The project that we promote is undertaken by Global Development Group (ABN57102400993) which is an ACNCregistered charity and an Australian Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade approved organisation in the overseas aid gift deduction scheme.

value: Friends of Samadhan holds fundraising initiatives during the course of the year, for the benefit of Samadhan, Delhi, its students and their families, staff and volunteers. This year we held a fundraiser to raise funds for Diwali gifts for students, staff and volunteers. These gifts are always practical, educational or nutritional. In March we again took a group of Vibrant Women Travel guests to Samadhan where they had a look around the Dakshinpuri Centre. We have found people are more inclined to donate if they have a personal experience and interaction with the Delhi based NGO.

value: We provide resources, information and education to parents, carers, early childcare workers and others who care for children, on the hazards children face and what can be done to prevent serious injuries occurring and minimise the severity of any injury. Kidsafe Qld hires, sells, checks and installs child car restraints throughout Queensland. We prepare programs and campaigns to alert the media, the authorities and the community at large about new and existing dangers, trends in injuries and the latest research and methods for reducing injury. Additionally we provide a onestop safety product shop located at Kidsafe House with an array of products on display and for sale to prevent injuries to babies, toddlers and children. Kidsafe Qld is an NDIS registered provider of services for children and adults with disabilities and medical conditions. By conducting playground safety checks we prevent children being injured or killed in playgrounds in kindergartens, schools and parks.

value: From JanuaryDecember 2024, HoMie ran two impact programs for young people affected by homelessness or hardship: The HoMie Pathway Alliance and the HoMie VIP Program. These programs are designed to equip them with the skills, confidence and experiences to be more workready and better prepared for their future. The VIP Program is HoMie s very first impact program, and one that it still runs to this day. The program is built around HoMie s VIP Days, where its store is closed to the public, and young people affected by homelessness or hardship are invited in to shop for free. Young people can choose up to five items of brandnew clothing off the racks, while enjoying haircuts, beauty services, and lunch with the HoMie team. These days are regularly facilitated by graduates of the HoMie Pathway Alliance, connecting attendees with a peer voice and a future opportunity. For young people who can t attend a VIP Day in person, HoMie works with their support service to send out a customised VIP Pack specially made for each individual young person, including five items of clothing, care packs, and handwritten notes from the HoMie team. In 2024, HoMie supported 423 young people, donating 1819 items of clothing. The HoMie Pathway Alliance is HoMie s flagship employment and education program. Over the course of eight months every year, young people affected by homelessness are paid to study a Cert III in Business and undertake professional and personal development classes, while being employed parttime at the HoMie store, or with one of HoMie s partners Champion, Nike, and Sportsgirl. value: Gateway Baptist Church & Community Centre continues to conduct weekly Church services on Sunday mornings, as well as some occasional Sunday evenings or other times. There are also a range of small group Bible Studies, Prayer Groups, Support Groups and Activity Groups run throughout the week. The Church conducts a Youth Group during School Terms, and a School Holiday Primary School Kids program. The Church is very much a familyfocused Church, and supports people from all walks of life, with extra general support provided to some of the more vulnerable in our community. The Church family financially supports a range of local, national and overseas Mission organisations/activities, as well as having an 'Emergency Relief' fund that can be called upon to assist people in need in our local community, as well as supporting national or international emergency relief situations. Weekly food distribution and community lunches are also now conducted, as well as programs to providing food/refreshments to vulnerable and disadvantaged people in the Hindmarsh and Adelaide CBD areas (assited via a State Government Grant). The Church's main income comes from the offerings/tithes/donations of members and Church attendees, with some additional income received from a small group of business tenants of our property, which continues to help pay off our loan as part of the 2017 Church expansion and redevelopment project.

value: Open Table s work significantly contributed to achieving its mission of providing equitable access to fresh, nutritious food and reducing food waste. Through initiatives like redistributing over 45.5 tonnes of surplus food and delivering 94 No Waste Cook Club workshops, the organization directly addressed food insecurity and empowered individuals with practical skills to minimize waste. Additionally, hosting 59 free community lunches and food markets fostered community connections, aligning with the goal of creating inclusive spaces. These efforts, supported by over 1,793 volunteer hours, demonstrate how Open Table s programs effectively meet its mission and aims.

value: The Columban Overseas Aid Fund (COAF) exists to express in practical ways the mission of the Columban Fathers: to stand in solidarity with the poor, the marginalised, and the vulnerable, and to promote justice, peace, and care for creation. Through COAF, the Columbans are able to channel the generosity of benefactors into programs that make a tangible difference in people s lives. Supporting the Mission in Action Direct Assistance to Communities in Need COAF provides resources for projects that address urgent human needs such as access to food, healthcare, housing, and education helping vulnerable families live with dignity. Education and Formation COAF assists in forming young people and faith communities to understand global inequalities, encouraging them to live out their faith through compassion and service. Promoting Justice and Solidarity Beyond material aid, COAF enables advocacy initiatives that tackle the root causes of poverty and exclusion, amplifying the voices of those too often unheard. The Impact Through these efforts, the Columban Overseas Aid Fund helps to achieve the Society s overall mission: proclaiming the Gospel through word and action, fostering crosscultural solidarity, and building communities where justice, peace, and care for creation are lived out daily.

value: Amaranth Foundation provided pro bono counselling, social and psychological support to vulnerable individuals in the community. Food insecurity was addressed by the provision of a free Food Rescue operation, as well as a social enterprise venture providing work and volunteering to people with disabilities. Amaranth also provide crisis and emergency accommodation as well as significantly subsidised accommodation for people with disabilities. Amaranth Foundation provides psychological support for people with Palliative and End of Life needs, or have advanced chronic health issues.

value: We continue to focus on identifying the best and brightest Australians seeking to undertake postgraduate studies to study at the University of Cambridge and to support them financially to achieve their ambitions. During 2024 Cambridge Australia Scholarships supported 27 scholars in residence across a range of Masters and PhD's and from a large number of disciplines. During 2024 Cambridge Australia Scholarships assessed 100 Masters applications and 49 PhD applications and from those awarded 6 Masters scholarships and 3 PhD's. The directors of CAS continue to focus on seeking new donors and support to award new post graduate scholarships nationally. For further information refer to our annual report available at: http://www.cambridgeaustralia.org.au/

value: The objective of the CTA funds is predominantly for the relief of suffering, distress, misfortune, or helplessness, giving freely to those who need such support and whose needs arouse compassion in the community. In 202324, to promote the health and wellbeing of the community, CTA supported physical activity by offering dance classes for women and children. To enhance mental health, CTA also provided free yoga classes. For refugee children lacking financial support for private educational assistance, CTA organised volunteers to offer free tuition. Operational expenses, such as stationery and other incidental costs for students and staff were covered by CTA. For refugees experiencing distress and misfortune because of their uncertain visa situations and mental distress, CTA provided support to obtain necessary legal assistance to discuss their visa issues.

value: CTA has donated $150.00 to Vanni Rehabilitation (Tears of Vanni) to give food to St Joseph Elders Home in Columbuthurai, Srilanka for its 40 th Anniversary. CTA has donated $1,606 worth of food to Home of Elderss in Mannar, Srilanka, St Joseph's Home for Elders in Trincomalee, Srilanka, Ramakrishna Mission in Batticaloa, Srilanka and Kurinchchi Children Home in Kilinochchi, Srilanka for its 40th Anniversary. CTA has donated $1,151 worth of food to Vanni Rehabilitation Organisation for the differently abled in Srilanka (VAROD) which primarily focuses on supporting and rehabilitating people with disablities. CTA has donated $1,924 to People Welfare Association Australia (PWAA) which provides financial and non-financial assistance or support to the diseased, disabled, sick, infirm, incurable, poor, destitute, helpless or unemployed persons, or the dependants of such persons. This assisted the relief of distress of those people occasioned by war, whether occasioned in SA or Srilanka.

value: We provided health and regulatory information, health education, advocacy and support to the medicinal cannabis sector, including patients, healthcare practitioners, industry and support organisations. We continued to provide educatiion through our online portal, providing access to RACGP accredited modules on all aspects of medicinal cannabis to members and nonmembers. We highlighted Medicinal Cannabis Awareness Week during the week of 1925 February to raise awareness of medicinal cannabis and to reduce stigma. ACMA continued to provide subgroups for its members to access support, education and networking opportunities for healthcare professionals (doctors, nurses and pharmacists) and expanded its industry subgroups to include one for manufacturers as well as the existing subassociation for cultivators. We also completed the pilot stage of our compassionate access scheme (COMPASS) and launched the full scale program to help patients unable to afford medicinal cannabis to access product. AMCA was also active in interacting with regulators (TGA, AHPRA) and the government to advocate for the sector.

value: The Corporation of the Diocesan Synod of North Queensland which was establised by an act of Parliament, covers a vast area from the Torres Straits in the North, to Normanton and Mt Isa in the West and South to Sarina. Our objective is to show the love and compassion of our Savior Jesus Christ. Some of our associated entities such as Schools and Anglicare are active across the Diocese, report in their own right because they are separately incorporated. These provide education opportunities to the public at large, while Anglicare provides services to the aged, infirmed and underprivileged. We have a number of indigenous ministries throughout the Cape and Torres Straits affording moral and spiritual guidance to all who seek help. The provision of financial assistance to indigent members of the community is a regular feature of our ministries across the Diocese. The free will offerings of the parishioners are expended in meeting these religious purposes.

value: Samaritan s Purse is a notforprofit, Christian organisation providing emergency relief and development assistance to suffering people around the world. Samaritan s Purse is meeting the physical needs of victims of war, famine, natural disaster, poverty and disease with the aim of demonstrating God s love and sharing the Good News of Jesus Christ. The aid and assistance are given without regard to the race, creed, gender, religion, or ethnicity of the beneficiaries. We do fundraising by means of social media, mailed and emailed newsletters and appeals as well as visiting churches and private schools. Funds are used to benefit people in developing countries with the following types of work: Education building of schools and training of teachers, literacy programs etc. Health building of clinics, training locals in health projects, sending medical teams from Australia Disaster Relief sending staff, volunteers and funding to countries affected by serious natural and manmade disasters Protection programs to train vulnerable people on how to migrate safely, programs to help returned migrants who have been exploited, training of villagers to earn incomes so as to avoid the necessity of migration Water providing communities access to clean water sources, build latrines and provide communities with hygiene training. Livelihoods the training of villagers on how best to raise farm animals and plant crops to create sustainability. In Australia we provide disaster relief in disasteraffected areas. We mobilise volunteers and staff to attend as second responders after a disaster.

value: RedR Australia is a unique NGO that identifies and deploys talented and experienced professionals during crises and conflict. We train people to be field ready for a multitude of emergencies and work with communities, governments, multilateral agencies, as well as local and international organisations. We strengthen our partners capability to prepare, respond and rebuild. Today, our roster of more than 1,230 experts (49% female) demonstrates 88 unique skillsets and 76 languages. They stand ready to deploy when the need arises. In FY24 RedR Australia: Deployed 126 specialists (49% female) to 36 host organisations in 45 countries across the Pacific, Asia, Middle East, Africa and Europe. Deployment duration averaged 5 months and collectively amounted to 662 months of support. Delivered 22 training courses to 557 participants in Australia, Fiji, Jordan Vanuatu, Indonesia and online. The average participant satisfaction rating was 94%. For more information, see FY24 Annual Report

value: The Australian Animal Cancer Foundation supports scientific research into cancer in companion animals such as dogs and cats. It funds equipment & expertise to treat animals with perexisting cancer, simultaneously documenting valuable clinical information to help uncover the mysteries of cancer in both animals and humans. The Foundation provides clinical trials ethically evaluating new treatments for animals with cancer translating fundamental scientific research from laboratory bench to the pet and to bedside human cancer patients. The Foundation also supports the education and training of research scientists, veterinarians and students
